senses.gloss: m. (preced.) appointment, permanency, institution; regular, perfunctory act.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3:12">Y. Ber. II, 4ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אכילת ק׳</he> a regular meal; <he>שינת ק׳</he> a regular sleep, v. <cite ref="P01241"><he>עַרְאַי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 4:1">Ber. IV, 1</cite> <he>תפלת … אין לה ק׳</he> for the evening prayer there is no fixed law, expl.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 4:4">Ib. IV, 4</cite> <he>העושה … ק׳ וכ׳</he> the prayer of one who treats it as a perfunctory obligation, is not a means of grace.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:13">Ab. II, 13</cite> <he>אל … ק׳ אלא רחמים וכ׳</he> make not thy prayer a perfunctory act, but a means of mercy and grace.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:15">Ib. I, 15</cite> <he>עשה תורתך ק׳</he> make thy study of the Law a regular engagement.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 2:1">Num. R. s. 2</cite>, beg. <he>משם … ק׳ שמתפללים וכ׳</he> from this the institution of three daily prayers is derived; a. fr.
